extracted.intended_audience: BBC staff, freelance presenters, producers, researchers, managers and independent production companies working for the BBC
extracted.subtask_description: Editorial guidelines specifying how conflicts of interest must be declared, managed and referred within the BBC, including mandatory referrals, managerial responsibilities and role‑specific restrictions to protect impartiality and the BBC's reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain audience trust and avoid undue outside influence
rubrics_metrics.description: Audiences must be able to trust the BBC and those working for it, and be confident that editorial decisions are not unduly affected by outside influences such as commercial or political activities or personal views or experiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how an individual's activities might affect the public's perception of the BBC and their role at the BBC; conflicts of interest can arise for anyone working for the BBC in any capacity, and risk damaging the BBC's brand and reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to declare personal interests
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a requirement that all BBC staff must formally declare any personal interest which may affect their work with the BBC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individuals are responsible for completing a Declaration of Personal Interests form; requirement extends to freelance presenters, reporters, producers and researchers and other workers; the onus to declare rests with the individual; particular sensitivities around on-air talent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Managers' responsibility to manage or mitigate conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Managers in each division are responsible for deciding what action, if any, is necessary to manage or mitigate potential conflicts of interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Managers must consider the wider implications for the BBC as a whole and may need to consider whether the positions of families and close personal contacts present a potential conflict of interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible restrictions on individuals' work where conflicts exist
rubrics_metrics.description: There may be times when individual freedoms need to be constrained or when managers decide that individuals may be restricted in the areas in which they can work, the times they can work or in certain aspects of their roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions depend on the kind of output involved, the individual's role, seniority and the nature of their personal interests and external activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ofcom regulation limited to due impartiality failures
rubrics_metrics.description: Conflicts of interest are not regulated by Ofcom, except where they may lead to a failure of due impartiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Ofcom Broadcasting Code Rule 5.8: Any personal interest of a reporter or presenter, which would call into question the due impartiality of the programme, must be made clear to the audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contractual obligation to comply with Editorial Guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The BBC's policy on personal interests forms part of the contract of employment that applies to its employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All contracts (staff or freelance) should include a requirement to comply with the Editorial Guidelines including Conflicts of Interest and, where applicable, Personal Use of Social Media; failure to comply may result in action and should be reflected in contracts for those otherwise engaged by the BBC, as well as being subject to the usual complaints process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application varies by role and output (higher standards for news/factual)
rubrics_metrics.description: The principles on conflicts of interest apply to everyone, but the application of the principles varies according to an individual's role and their level of involvement with BBC content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reflects audience expectations of impartiality and integrity, particularly that news and current affairs and factual journalism meet the highest levels of accuracy and impartiality; factual journalism refers to journalistic content produced outside news and current affairs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional constraints for financial journalism and advice output
rubrics_metrics.description: There are additional legal and regulatory constraints on those involved in financial journalism or those who are involved in output offering financial or consumer advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such legal/regulatory constraints may impose stricter limits or requirements beyond these Guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted use of staff with expertise and union activities
rubrics_metrics.description: These Guidelines are not intended to prevent the BBC from using staff, freelances and presenters with expertise or specialisms in particular areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also not intended to prevent elected officials of the BBC's recognised trade unions carrying out legitimate activities on behalf of their union.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference to other relevant guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: This section must be read in conjunction with the section on Impartiality and the detailed guidance on Conflicts of Interest and Personal Use of Social Media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section 2 Impartiality and the separate guidance documents 'Conflicts of Interest' and 'Personal Use of Social Media'.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.2.1: No influence or reasonable perception of influence on editorial judgements
rubrics_metrics.description: An individual's political, commercial, financial or other external interests must not influence, or be reasonably perceived as having influenced, BBC editorial judgements.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.2.2: No material connection with featured organisations without prior referral
rubrics_metrics.description: Those involved in any role in the creation of BBC content must have no material connection with products, businesses or other organisations featured or reflected in that content, nor with their competitors or in some cases with the relevant business sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such a connection exists, prior referral must be made to Editorial Policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.2.3: Maintain BBC editorial control where presenters have production company roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Where on-air presenters or others used in an on-air role such as team captains, hosts, judges, or their agents, own or have senior management positions in independent production companies making output for the BBC, the BBC must maintain overall editorial control of all aspects of the content, including marketing and promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory referrals must be made in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Mandatory referrals are an essential part of the BBC's editorial and compliance process and must be observed; mandatory referrals must be referred in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referrals route matters to Director Editorial Policy and Standards or other senior editorial figures as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.1: News/current affairs presenters must not front charity/campaigning campaigns
rubrics_metrics.description: News and current affairs presenters should not front campaigns for charities or campaigning bodies as this could compromise the BBC's reputation for impartiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any proposal that would not comply must be referred to Director Editorial Policy and Standards. (See 4.4.26)

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.2: External media training by news/current affairs/factual staff normally prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals involved in the production or presentation of BBC news and current affairs and factual journalism output should not normally undertake external media training work, including for commercial companies, charities and campaign groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any proposal must be referred to their line manager in advance and referred to Director Editorial Policy and Standards. (See 4.4.33)

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.3: Unique-access/content by talent requires strong editorial justification and referral
rubrics_metrics.description: There may be circumstances where it is not possible to produce content about a specific personality or area unless it is produced by an independent production company owned by, or as a co-production with, that talent or an associated agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such proposal will require strong editorial justification and must be referred to the relevant divisional director and Editorial Policy; Director Editorial Policy and Standards must also be consulted. (See 4.4.46)

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.4: Public expression of opinions on public policy or politics must be declared
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual in a role requiring impartiality who intends to express opinions publicly on matters of current public policy, politics or any controversial issue, or take part in political activity, must inform their line manager in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line manager should consult Chief Adviser Politics if there is a risk to impartiality or the perception of impartiality. (See Section 2 Impartiality: 2.4.14)

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.5: Prompt reporting of newly identified potential conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an individual considers a potential conflict has arisen that they have not already declared, they must inform their line manager promptly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial Policy may also be consulted. (See 4.4.4)

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.6: Early referral for portfolio careers
rubrics_metrics.description: Where people who work for the BBC develop portfolio careers involving external roles, early referral to a senior editorial figure is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorial Policy may be consulted. (See 4.4.5)

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.7: Consult Editorial Policy where material connection exists with featured organisations
rubrics_metrics.description: Where there is a material connection between anyone who has a role in the creation of BBC content with products, businesses or other organisations featured or reflected in that content Editorial Policy must be consulted in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.8: In specialist areas ensure editorial procedures to avoid conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: In some areas – such as specialist music, arts, sport, science or lifestyle programming – on-air presenters and talent, commissioning and production staff, and other teams who support them, may have commercial, professional and external personal interests in their area of expertise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The relevant division should ensure appropriate editorial procedures are in place so there is no conflict of interest with their BBC role; Editorial Policy must be consulted. (See 4.4.9)

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.9: Consult Chief Adviser Politics at outset for potential political impartiality risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Chief Adviser Politics must be consulted at the outset if there is any possibility of political activity being perceived as a risk to BBC impartiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judgements will reflect individual circumstances including type of activity and the nature of the individual's BBC role. (See 4.4.21-4.4.23)

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.10: Notify line manager and consult Chief Adviser Politics before seeking political candidacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual who intends to seek nomination as a party candidate for election at national or local level, or intends declaring publicly their independent candidacy, must notify their line manager in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Line manager should consult the Chief Adviser Politics before the intention is made public. (See 4.4.22)

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.11: Proposals to work for or be publicly associated with charities/campaigning groups must be referred
rubrics_metrics.description: Any proposal by individuals, including presenters of flagship programmes, to work for, or be publicly associated with, charities, campaigning or lobbying groups must be referred to the head of department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The head of department must consult Editorial Policy. (See 4.4.25)

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.12: Proposals to write external columns or blogs must be referred
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals involved in the production or presentation of news and current affairs output and factual journalism output must refer proposals to write columns or blog posts for external publications to a senior editorial figure in the relevant division.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes freelances primarily known as BBC news presenters or reporters and individuals involved in production of factual journalism. (See 4.4.28)

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.13: Consulting line manager before public comment on BBC matters
rubrics_metrics.description: Any individual commenting publicly, including on social media, on BBC matters or stories, or issues concerning other broadcasters or broadcasting policy, must consult their line manager in advance, unless it comes within their professional remit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See Section 2 Impartiality: 2.4.15

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.14: Permission required before providing media training
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals involved in the production or presentation of editorial content for the BBC must obtain permission from their line manager before agreeing to provide media training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Freelance presenters must disclose their training work where it may be a conflict of interest with their work for the BBC. (See 4.4.32)

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.15: Do not accept personal benefits from organisations with BBC dealings
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals must not accept personal benefits, or benefits for their family or close personal relations, from organisations or people with whom they might have dealings on the BBC's behalf.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unacceptable benefits include goods, discounts, services, cash, loans, gratuities or entertainment, including tickets, outside the normal scope of business hospitality; any exception that could affect production of content must be referred to the relevant head of department who should normally consult Editorial Policy. (See 4.4.34)

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.16: Restrictions on presenters promoting certain products or services
rubrics_metrics.description: On-air presenters and others used in an on-air role must not promote tobacco products or adult services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any proposal for them to promote other products or services that may risk damaging the BBC's reputation, such as gambling, alcohol and vaping products must be referred to a senior editorial figure. (See 4.4.35)

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.17: Promotional work for occasional/limited factual contributors must be referred
rubrics_metrics.description: Where an individual used in front of the camera/microphone is engaged on a limited or occasional basis in factual output, any proposal to undertake promotional work must be referred in advance to the head of department.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Head of department should consult Editorial Policy. (See 4.4.38-4.4.39)

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.18: Commercial relationships for factual presenters require editorial procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: In some factual programmes, on-air presenters and others with expertise in their field may have associated commercial relationships.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where there is any proposal for those individuals to undertake external promotional activity, the relevant division should ensure appropriate editorial procedures are in place so there is no conflict with their BBC role; Editorial Policy must be consulted. (See 4.4.40)

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.19: Recreating factual roles in fictional output requires referral
rubrics_metrics.description: Presenters of factual output may be asked to recreate their roles in fictional output; this may risk confusing audiences and compromise the credibility of their own output.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any such proposal must be referred to their head of department. (See 4.4.45)

rubrics_metrics.name: 4.3.20: News presenters should not appear as news presenters in fictional bulletins if confusing
rubrics_metrics.description: Current presenters of BBC news output should not appear as news presenters in a fictional bulletin if there is a reasonable possibility that this could confuse or mislead audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any proposal to do so, for example in a dramatic, comic, unrealistic or fantasy situation, must be referred to their head of department. (See 4.4.45)
